title: Paides dyo
about: Xenophon opens his story of the Ten Thousand, the Greek army that marched into Persia, with a royal family feud: two brothers, one throne, and a mother with a favourite.

badge.name: Sibling Rivalry
badge.about: Read the opening of Xenophon's Anabasis

lines.g: Δαρείου καὶ Παρυσάτιδος γίγνονται παῖδες δύο
lines.t: Dareiou kai Parysatidos gignontai paides dyo,
lines.en: Darius and Parysatis had two sons,

q.prompt: How many sons did Darius and Parysatis have?

lines.g: πρεσβύτερος μὲν Ἀρταξέρξης νεώτερος δὲ Κῦρος
lines.t: presbyteros men Artaxerxēs, neōteros de Kyros.
lines.en: the elder Artaxerxes, the younger Cyrus.

q.prompt: Which son was the elder?

lines.g: ἐπεὶ δὲ ἠσθένει Δαρεῖος καὶ ὑπώπτευε τελευτὴν τοῦ βίου
lines.t: epei de ēsthenei Dareios kai hypōpteue teleutēn tou biou,
lines.en: When Darius fell ill and sensed that the end of his life was near,

lines.g: ἐβούλετο τὼ παῖδε ἀμφοτέρω παρεῖναι
lines.t: ebouleto tō paide amphoterō pareinai.
lines.en: he wanted both his sons to be with him.

lines.g: ὁ μὲν οὖν πρεσβύτερος παρὼν ἐτύγχανε
lines.t: ho men oun presbyteros parōn etynchane;
lines.en: The elder happened to be there already;

lines.g: Κῦρον δὲ μεταπέμπεται ἀπὸ τῆς ἀρχῆς ἧς αὐτὸν σατράπην ἐποίησε
lines.t: Kyron de metapempetai apo tēs archēs hēs auton satrapēn epoiēse.
lines.en: Cyrus he sent for from the province he had made him satrap of.

q.prompt: Where was Cyrus when his father sent for him?

lines.g: ἐπεὶ δὲ ἐτελεύτησε Δαρεῖος καὶ κατέστη εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν Ἀρταξέρξης
lines.t: epei de eteleutēse Dareios kai katestē eis tēn basileian Artaxerxēs,
lines.en: When Darius died and Artaxerxes was installed as king,

lines.g: Τισσαφέρνης διαβάλλει τὸν Κῦρον πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν ὡς ἐπιβουλεύοι αὐτῷ
lines.t: Tissaphernēs diaballei ton Kyron pros ton adelphon hōs epibouleuoi autōi.
lines.en: Tissaphernes slandered Cyrus to his brother, claiming he was plotting against him.

q.prompt: What did Tissaphernes tell the new king?

lines.g: ὁ δὲ πείθεται καὶ συλλαμβάνει Κῦρον ὡς ἀποκτενῶν
lines.t: ho de peithetai kai syllambanei Kyron hōs apoktenōn;
lines.en: The king believed it and arrested Cyrus, meaning to put him to death;

lines.g: ἡ δὲ μήτηρ ἐξαιτησαμένη αὐτὸν ἀποπέμπει πάλιν ἐπὶ τὴν ἀρχήν
lines.t: hē de mētēr exaitēsamenē auton apopempei palin epi tēn archēn.
lines.en: but their mother begged for his life and sent him back to his province.

q.prompt: Who saved Cyrus?

title: Alōpēx kai botrys
about: Aesop's fable of the fox and the grapes, the origin of 'sour grapes'. The fables circulated for centuries before being written down in plain prose like this.

badge.name: Sour Grapes
badge.about: Read Aesop's fable of the fox and the grapes

lines.g: ἀλώπηξ λιμώττουσα ὡς ἐθεάσατο ἀπό τινος ἀναδενδράδος βότρυας κρεμαμένους
lines.t: alōpēx limōttousa, hōs etheasato apo tinos anadendrados botryas kremamenous,
lines.en: A hungry fox, when she saw bunches of grapes hanging from a vine on a tree,

lines.g: ἠβουλήθη αὐτῶν περιγενέσθαι καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο
lines.t: ēboulēthē autōn perigenesthai kai ouk ēdynato.
lines.en: wanted to get hold of them, but could not.

q.prompt: Did the fox get the grapes?

lines.g: ἀπαλλαττομένη δὲ πρὸς ἑαυτὴν εἶπεν
lines.t: apallattomenē de pros heautēn eipen:
lines.en: As she went away, she said to herself:

lines.g: ὄμφακές εἰσιν
lines.t: omphakes eisin.
lines.en: “They're unripe.”

lines.g: οὕτω καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἔνιοι τῶν πραγμάτων ἐφικέσθαι μὴ δυνάμενοι
lines.t: houtō kai tōn anthrōpōn enioi tōn pragmatōn ephikesthai mē dynamenoi
lines.en: So too some people, when they cannot achieve what they want

lines.g: δι᾽ ἀσθένειαν τοὺς καιροὺς αἰτιῶνται
lines.t: di' astheneian tous kairous aitiōntai.
lines.en: through their own weakness, blame the circumstances.

q.prompt: What is the moral?
options: people blame circumstances for their own failures

title: Mēnin aeide
about: The first lines of European literature. Homer asks the Muse to sing of the anger of Achilles and the deaths it caused. His Greek is older than Attic, so expect some strange forms.

badge.name: Rhapsode
badge.about: Read the opening of Homer's Iliad

lines.g: μῆνιν ἄειδε θεὰ Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος
lines.t: mēnin aeide, thea, Pēlēiadeō Achilēos
lines.en: Sing, goddess, the wrath of Achilles, son of Peleus,

lines.g: οὐλομένην ἣ μυρί᾽ Ἀχαιοῖς ἄλγε᾽ ἔθηκε
lines.t: oulomenēn, hē myri' Achaiois alge' ethēke,

lines.g: πολλὰς δ᾽ ἰφθίμους ψυχὰς Ἄϊδι προΐαψεν

lines.en: and hurled many mighty souls down to Hades,

lines.g: ἡρώων αὐτοὺς δὲ ἑλώρια τεῦχε κύνεσσιν

lines.g: οἰωνοῖσί τε πᾶσι Διὸς δ᾽ ἐτελείετο βουλή

lines.en: and for all the birds, and the will of Zeus was being done,

lines.g: ἐξ οὗ δὴ τὰ πρῶτα διαστήτην ἐρίσαντε
lines.t: ex hou dē ta prōta diastētēn erisante
lines.en: from the moment the two first quarrelled and parted,

lines.t: Atreidēs te anax andrōn kai dios Achilleus.
lines.en: Atreus' son, lord of men, and godlike Achilles.

title: Historiēs apodexis
about: Herodotus opens the first great work of Greek history by saying why he wrote it. He writes in Ionic, not Attic: notice ἱστορίης for ἱστορίας, θωμαστά for θαυμαστά and datives in -οισι. A 'barbarian' was simply anyone who did not speak Greek.

badge.name: Father of History
badge.about: Read the opening of Herodotus' Histories

lines.g: Ἡροδότου Ἁλικαρνησσέος ἱστορίης ἀπόδεξις ἥδε
lines.t: Hērodotou Halikarnēsseos historiēs apodexis hēde,
lines.en: This is the presentation of the inquiry of Herodotus of Halicarnassus,

lines.g: ὡς μήτε τὰ γενόμενα ἐξ ἀνθρώπων τῷ χρόνῳ ἐξίτηλα γένηται
lines.t: hōs mēte ta genomena ex anthrōpōn tōi chronōi exitēla genētai,
lines.en: so that what people have done may not fade with time,

q.prompt: Why does Herodotus write?
options: so that the past is not forgotten
to win a prize at Olympia

lines.g: μήτε ἔργα μεγάλα τε καὶ θωμαστά
lines.t: mēte erga megala te kai thōmasta,
lines.en: and so that great and marvellous deeds,

lines.g: τὰ μὲν Ἕλλησι τὰ δὲ βαρβάροισι ἀποδεχθέντα ἀκλεᾶ γένηται
lines.t: ta men Hellēsi ta de barbaroisi apodechthenta, aklea genētai,
lines.en: some performed by Greeks and some by barbarians, may not lose their fame,

q.prompt: Whose achievements will he record?
options: those of Greeks and barbarians alike

lines.g: τά τε ἄλλα καὶ δι᾽ ἣν αἰτίην ἐπολέμησαν ἀλλήλοισι
lines.t: ta te alla kai di' hēn aitiēn epolemēsan allēloisi.
lines.en: and above all, the reason why they went to war with each other.

q.prompt: What question will the work answer above all?
options: why Greeks and barbarians went to war

title: Pollakis ethaumasa
about: Xenophon, who had known Socrates as a young man, sets out to defend his teacher's memory. He begins with the charges on which Athens condemned Socrates to death in 399 BC. Watch the participles: Socrates 'does wrong' by not recognising, bringing in and corrupting.

badge.name: Character Witness
badge.about: Read the opening of Xenophon's Memorabilia

lines.g: πολλάκις ἐθαύμασα τίσι ποτὲ λόγοις Ἀθηναίους ἔπεισαν
lines.t: pollakis ethaumasa tisi pote logois Athēnaious epeisan
lines.en: I have often wondered by what arguments they persuaded the Athenians,

q.prompt: What does Xenophon say about the verdict?
options: he has often wondered how it happened

lines.g: οἱ γραψάμενοι Σωκράτην ὡς ἄξιος εἴη θανάτου τῇ πόλει
lines.t: hoi grapsamenoi Sōkratēn hōs axios eiē thanatou tēi polei.
lines.en: those who indicted Socrates, that he deserved death at the city's hands.

lines.g: ἡ μὲν γὰρ γραφὴ κατ᾽ αὐτοῦ τοιάδε τις ἦν
lines.t: hē men gar graphē kat' autou toiade tis ēn:
lines.en: The indictment against him ran something like this:

lines.g: ἀδικεῖ Σωκράτης οὓς μὲν ἡ πόλις νομίζει θεοὺς οὐ νομίζων
lines.t: adikei Sōkratēs hous men hē polis nomizei theous ou nomizōn,
lines.en: Socrates does wrong by not recognising the gods the city recognises,

lines.g: ἕτερα δὲ καινὰ δαιμόνια εἰσφέρων

lines.g: ἀδικεῖ δὲ καὶ τοὺς νέους διαφθείρων

lines.en: he also does wrong by corrupting the young.

q.prompt: What is the second charge?

title: Ho anexetastos bios
about: Plato's version of Socrates' speech at his trial. Found guilty, Socrates must propose his own penalty. Why not go into exile and live quietly? This is his answer, and it ends in his most famous line.

badge.name: Gadfly
badge.about: Read Socrates on the unexamined life

lines.g: ἐάντε γὰρ λέγω ὅτι τῷ θεῷ ἀπειθεῖν τοῦτ᾽ ἐστὶν
lines.t: eante gar legō hoti tōi theōi apeithein tout' estin
lines.en: For if I say that this would mean disobeying the god

lines.g: καὶ διὰ τοῦτ᾽ ἀδύνατον ἡσυχίαν ἄγειν
lines.t: kai dia tout' adynaton hēsychian agein,

lines.g: καὶ ἐμαυτὸν καὶ ἄλλους ἐξετάζοντος

lines.g: ὁ δὲ ἀνεξέταστος βίος οὐ βιωτὸς ἀνθρώπῳ
